question: Will the S&P 500 close above 7,710 on Friday?
resolution_criteria:
Resolution criteria

This market will resolve to YES if the S&P 500 Index (SPX) daily closing price is strictly above 7,710.00 on Friday, September 4, 2026. It will resolve to NO if the index closes at or below 7,710.00.

The primary source of truth for the index's closing price will be Yahoo Finance (^GSPC) or, as a secondary source, Google Finance (INDEXSP: .INX).

If U.S. stock markets are unexpectedly closed on Friday, September 4, 2026, this market will resolve based on the closing price of the next official trading day.

Background

The S&P 500 index ended trading on Friday, August 28, 2026, at 7,711.76. The close marked a weekly gain of 0.49% and brought the index’s month-to-date return to nearly 3%, continuing a historically strong setup for the latter part of the year. However, comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole, signaling a willingness to tighten monetary policy further to combat inflation, have introduced some near-term volatility and raised expectations for a September rate hike.

## Research brief: Will the S&P 500 close above 7,710 on Friday, Sept 4, 2026?

The index needs to close above 7,710.00. The last close I could confirm was 7,631.47 on Sept 1, so it would need to gain about 1.0% from there. Friday's August jobs report is the main event that could move it.

### 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't fetch Yahoo Finance (^GSPC) or Google Finance directly; the proxy refused the connection. The figures below come from secondary reports.
- 2026-08-28: The S&P 500 closed at 7,711.76, down 0.3% on the day after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. [local10/AP](https://www.local10.com/business/2026/08/28/us-stocks-drift-after-expectations-rise-for-the-fed-to-hike-rates-to-get-inflation-under-control/)
- 2026-08-31: YCharts lists a close of 7,686.14 (high 7,697.52, low 7,665.06). Only one source gives this. [YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indices/^SPX/level)
- 2026-09-01: The close was 7,631.47, down 0.71%, per CNBC and AAP/CommBank. One other report (MTC) gives 7,645.75, down 0.53%, so treat that figure with caution. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/stock-market-today-live-updates.html), [CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/09/wall-street-falls-as-oil-and-bond-yields-rise.html), [MTC](https://www.metatradingclub.com/?p=25195)
- 2026-09-02: A CNBC page reportedly shows a Sept 2 close of 7,666.60, up 0.46%. That close would have come after the 14:02 UTC forecast deadline, and I couldn't verify it. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The index is about 1.0% below the threshold (7,631.47 against 7,710), or about 0.6% below if the unverified 7,666.60 Sept 2 close is right.
- 2026-09-01: That was the third straight down session. [Schaeffer's](https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/ezines/2026/09/01/stocks-slide-into-september-as-inflation-fears-lift-yields)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-02: ADP private payrolls came in at +38K against +47K expected, the lowest since January. [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/preview-us-nonfarm-payrolls-are-due-on-4th-september-at-1330bst0830edt)
- 2026-09-01: Renewed US-Iran hostilities and tanker disruption in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent above $95. WTI settled at $90.22, up 5.5%. [Proactive](https://proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1097916/inflation-iran-and-interest-rates-weigh-on-sentiment-ahead-of-the-bell-on-wall-street-1097916.html?.tsrc=rss), [Schaeffer's](https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/ezines/2026/09/01/stocks-slide-into-september-as-inflation-fears-lift-yields)
- 2026-09-01: The 10-year Treasury yield hit about 4.78% intraday, its highest since January 2025, and the 30-year was near 5.27%. Tech and growth stocks led the decline, and the Nasdaq fell about 1%. [Proactive](https://proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1097916/inflation-iran-and-interest-rates-weigh-on-sentiment-ahead-of-the-bell-on-wall-street-1097916.html?.tsrc=rss), [CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/09/wall-street-falls-as-oil-and-bond-yields-rise.html)
- 2026-09-01: The VIX rose; Sharecast reports a 9.6% jump. [Schaeffer's](https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/ezines/2026/09/01/stocks-slide-into-september-as-inflation-fears-lift-yields), [HL](https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/market-reports/us-close-stocks-drop-on-bond-sell-off,-oil-price-surge)
- 2026-08-28: Warsh kept the possibility of a hike open at Jackson Hole, and markets raised the odds of a hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. [vermoegenszentrum](https://www.vermoegenszentrum.ch/en/stock-exchange-and-markets/news/markets-now-see-higher-rates-after-warsh-speech), [Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/stocks-mixed-ahead-fed-chair-warsh)

### 4. Base rates
- Recent closes: 7,711.76 (Aug 28), 7,686.14 (Aug 31), 7,631.47 (Sept 1). The short-term trend is down, but August as a whole gained nearly 3%.
- Rough volatility estimate (my own, not from a source): with daily moves of roughly 0.7-1% and the VIX elevated, three trading days (Sept 2-4) imply a typical move of about 1.2-1.7%. A gain of 1.0% or more from the Sept 1 close is therefore roughly a 0.6-0.8 standard deviation move.
- Seasonality: September is historically the weakest month for the S&P 500, and early September often turns down after a strong August. I didn't find a specific 2026 source quantifying this.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi lists an S&P 500 above/below contract for 4pm EDT on Sept 4 (KXINXU-26SEP04H1600). I couldn't find its price as of the forecast deadline. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxinxu/sp-500-abovebelow/kxinxu-26sep04h1600)
- 30rates.com had a model forecast of about 7,786 for late August. It is a low-quality source. [30rates](https://30rates.com/sp500)
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold price for this exact strike.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-04, 08:30 ET: The August jobs report. Consensus is about +56-58K payrolls (range -25K to +121K) and unemployment around 4.1%, after July's -23K. BMO data says the August headline has come in below estimates 71% of the time. Benchmark revisions last week reduced job counts through March. [InvestingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/preview-august-non-farm-payrolls-by-the-numbers/), [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/preview-us-nonfarm-payrolls-are-due-on-4th-september-at-1330bst0830edt)
- Sept 3: Weekly jobless claims and the ISM services report. These dates are from the usual calendar; I didn't confirm them.
- Ongoing: Oil and the US-Iran situation around Hormuz, plus Treasury yields near multi-month highs.
- The market is open on Sept 4. Labor Day falls on Monday, Sept 7, so Friday is a pre-holiday session that may have lighter volume.
- The next FOMC meeting is Sept 15-16, after resolution, but Fed speakers' comments this week could move hike expectations.
